text:
Devon: quick idea dump  We should try a control-plane partition for Private customers: tiny in-VPC control plane that owns tenant auth & egress leases, and a global CP that keeps policy, billing, and audit. Goal: lower blast radius and enable local egress with source-ip preservation.
Maria: sounds promising. main worry is cert propagation and the cutover window. last time a peering flip caused a 20-40s error burst.
Alex: what about a two-phase cutover flow? PREPARE where local CP allocates IPs and syncs state, runs health probes; ACTIVATE flips the dataplane pointer. fallback to global CP on failure.
Sam: for src-ip preservation, the orchestrator must control ephemeral IP leases and a sticky SNAT table. ENIs per tenant are expensive. SNAT + sticky map seems more realistic but we need persistence across failovers.
Priya: do we enforce a sidecar that holds route state in each tenant VPC? sidecar simplifies dataplane changes but adds maintenance. lightweight agent + relay might be a better ops tradeoff.
Devon: leaning agent + relay. propose a PREPARE->ACTIVATE->REVOKE state machine. PREPARE: allocate lease, fetch certs, dual-write mapping to global CP but don't switch dataplane. ACTIVATE: flip route to local path. REVOKE for rollbacks.
Alex: add probes in PREPARE: tcp handshake + small TLS echo to ensure certs are valid. mark PREPARE as failing if probes fail.
Maria: certs should be short-lived (e.g., 5 min) and monotonic (sequence numbers) to prevent replay. also include a cert_seq in audit logs.
Sam: mapping replication must be low-latency. dual-write with a compact per-tenant changelog seems reasonable. avoid large per-request fanouts.
Priya: question: how do we keep conntrack/session continuity during handoff? if mapping diverges briefly, existing TCP sessions might stall. possible mitigations: conntrack export (hard), or a short grace window where both paths accept packets for N secs.
Devon: conntrack export across accounts is messy. implement a polite handoff: for N seconds after ACTIVATE, old path will RST long-lived connections to force reconnects quickly, and new path accepts new flows. reduces stalls.
Alex: also emit metrics: preactivate_probe_ok, replication_lag_ms_p50/p95, activate_rollback_rate. dashboard alerts on probe failures and replication lag > 200ms.
Maria: rollout plan: enable PREPARE/dual-write for 5% of tenants (label: egress-canary=true), monitor for 48h; then enable ACTIVATE for that cohort; keep fallback to global CP for 24h post-activate.
Sam: I'll spike replication with a harness: write 10k synthetic mappings and measure replication tail. want to know p99 latency and jitter.
Priya: add operator CLI: `rictl egress prepare --tenant T --dry-run` and `rictl egress activate --lease L`. include `--simulate-probes`.
Devon: API sketch: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/egress/leases {"mode":"dual-write"} -> returns lease_id + prebuilt_probe_plan. POST /v1/tenants/{id}/egress/leases/{lease_id}/activate -> returns activation status.
Alex: ensure KMS scope is minimized: local CP gets ephemeral wrapping keys only; signing should be audited and global CP retains audit log copy.
Maria: add tests for cert monotonicity and replay attempts. Priya, add that to the checklist.
Priya: done. also adding a dashboard card for "pre-activate probe failures" and an SLO for activation rollback < 1% per 24h.
infra-bot: Job queued: egress-replication-spike (id job-9034).
Devon: thanks. @Maria @Sam please post the measurements into the RFC doc once you have them. we'll review in arch sync tomorrow 10am PT. :thumbsup:
Alex: one more thought: cost analysis ENI vs SNAT table vs operational complexity. add to RFC.
Devon: I'll draft the follow-up RFC section with the PREPARE/ACTIVATE state machine and cutover playbook. aim to post EOD.
